newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIAN STATE BANK EYES UP TO $100 MLN EUROBONDS.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIAN STATE BANK EYES UP TO $100 MLN EUROBONDS.

text.p: Romanian state bank Banca Comerciala Romana SA (BCR) plans to raise up to $100 million in Eurobonds on the international capital markets early next year through Merrill Lynch International .

"The concrete conditions will be worked up after getting a rating. We plan to raise between $60 to $100 million," BCR president Ion Ghica said after he signed a letter of agreement with Winthrop Smith, president of the U.S. investment bank.

Ghica said the planned issue, the first non-government guaranteed raising by a Romanian bank or company, is likely to be launched in January or February next year. Its expected maturity is three years.

The BCR, which specialised in industry financing before the 1989 fall of communism, was reshaped in December 1990. It continue to manage the bulk of loans granted to industrial companies and its network is one of the strongest in Romania.
Its share capital is 225.4 billion lei and assets top 4.7 trillion lei. Its rating for short-term local currency debt, awarded by Thomson BankWatch, is LC1.

Merrill Lynch has already handled two medium-term issues on capital markets for the National Bank -- a $50 million private placement last November and $225 million worth of three-year Eurobonds in June. It has also advised Romania in getting its first credit ratings earlier this year.
"The important part of the strategy was to not only raise funds for the government but also to set benchmarks for other sectors of the economy," Winthrop said.

Merrill Lynch is also arranging the first foreign issue by a Romanian city by helping Bucharest authorities raise up to $200 million through a private placement and autumn municipal bonds to upgrade infrastructure.
"It (the deal) is subject to diligences and the approval of the government," Winthrop said.
He said said his company also sees electricity authority Renel RA as one of the Romanian companies suitable to go on the international markets.

Romania was awarded a BB-plus score, by Japan Credit Rating agency, somewhat higher than the BB- minus ratings of Standards and Poors and IBCA and the BA-three from Moody's Investors Service. ($=3,176)
